text:
leila: Small smoke check result from onboarding rf-7b-v2-alt (candidate model) against the onboarding-holdout set. Noting because it's weird.
harry: what's odd?
leila: NDCG@10 shows +0.7% vs baseline but MRR@1 drops by 1.2%. Looks like better tail ordering but worse top1.
alicia: curious. Could be that the model is smoothing scores, pushing the previously narrow top1 margin down. Any slices?
leila: yes, navigational queries (explicit page names) have top1 regressions, while exploratory queries gain.
ben: we should avoid flipping top1 for nav queries. How many examples?
leila: top1-change fraction for nav = 4.4% of nav queries, overall top1-change = 1.1%.
jira-bot: Created ticket #REINF-432: investigate rf-7b-v2-alt onboarding top1 regressions.
leila: I'm going to extract 50 nav query failures and upload to the review doc. Also running per-query score diffs.
alicia: flagging metric: "nav_top1_breaks" as a gating metric for onboarding.
harry: good. Also check candidate pool composition - different pooling can lead to top1 swaps.
leila: we used k=50 candidates from retrieval. I'll add a k=200 run.
ben: thanks, will follow the ticket.
